clue.text: Old coin, one blocking vent

indicators.note: to block something is to sit inside it, plugging it up, so one piece lodges within the other

explanation.surface: An antique coin has got stuck in an air vent.
explanation.walkthrough: A ducat was a gold or silver coin used across medieval Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat is a historical European currency piece, so it is an example of an old coin.

clue.text: Discussion not up to be raised before closing parts of summit conference

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: someone still abed is in bed, not up

indicators.note: closing parts are the final letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A discussion is put off until the very end of a summit conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not up' looks like a phrase about the debate; it stands for ABED, an old word for in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion in which opposing arguments are put forward.

clue.text: Unusually competent, suppressing Right with singular argument

indicators.note: something done unusually is done in an unexpected way, so the letters fall into an unfamiliar order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly capable silences the right wing in a one-on-one argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suppressing' suggests R goes inside, but the whole lot is shuffled together, so its position does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is a minor dispute or disagreement, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Panic about count I ran perversely having mistake in the maths

indicators.note: acting perversely means behaving contrarily, so the letters come out in a wayward order
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

explanation.surface: Someone panics after getting a count wrong and making a mistake in their sums.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit after the first letter of the word for panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncation error arises in calculation when a number is cut short rather than taken in full, a mathematical inaccuracy.

clue.text: Article recording introduction from historian supports collections of letters

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: an introduction is the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: abets means aids or backs up

explanation.surface: A historian's article backs up a set of letters, perhaps an archive of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests correspondence, but here it means the characters of a writing system.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is the full set of characters used to write a language, so alphabets are sets of these.

clue.text: Political group out of power supporting the creative industries

indicators.note: something out of a group has left it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A political party out of office pledges backing for the creative industries.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone keenly interested in, and keen to promote, the arts, a loose fit for backing creative work.

clue.text: Frenchman, perhaps, showing skill for one in theatrical area

indicators.note: X for Y means X takes the place of Y, so one letter is swapped out for a word

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Frenchman shows talent and performs in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The ART replaces the I in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is the part of a theatre auditorium behind the orchestra stalls, the pit area.

clue.text: What could give cinema a darn toot? Where's Yosemite Sam when you need him?

definitions.text: Where's Yosemite Sam when you need him?

indicators.note: asking what could give these letters invites the solver to rearrange them into something else

explanation.surface: A grumble about a noisy cinema, wishing a gun-toting cowboy would appear to silence it.
explanation.walkthrough: Yosemite Sam is the pistol-firing cowboy in Warner Bros' Looney Tunes shorts, so you find him in a film of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite Sam is a Looney Tunes character, so the place you would look for him is a piece of cartoon film.

clue.text: Amphibian departed, abandoning lake

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A frog or newt has left its lake behind.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, and newts are amphibians.

clue.text: Discussion of work, hard work, interrupting attempt to follow game

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to stalk is to track an animal being hunted
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard, and an op is an opus, a work

explanation.surface: Talk about the job is broken off by a hunting expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is not a sport here but animals that are hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop talk is conversation about one's job or trade, especially outside working hours.

clue.text: Prevent one leaving less riotous feaster

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Stopping someone from walking out makes a raucous diner calmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A banqueter is someone who takes part in a banquet, a lavish feast.

clue.text: Opening extracted from report Nixon backed

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the letters read in the opposite direction
extracted from means pulled out of the run of letters in the words that follow

parts.note: the letters inside the two words

explanation.surface: The opening of a report endorsed by President Nixon.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the introductory or opening section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Henry to appear in a short time — and again and again?

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be found inside it

parts.note: in a trice means in a moment
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry turns up briefly, then again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a man's name but stands for the physics unit. The definition counts: once, and again, and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something thrice means doing it three times: once, then a second time, then a third.

clue.text: Relative getting taxman releasing money unexpectedly — a source of ease

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to release something is to let it go, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: rel. is the abbreviation for relative
M is a common abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A relative who gets an unexpected tax refund finds it very soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A relaxant is a drug or other agent that relieves tension, so it brings ease.

clue.text: Compiler is busy tonight also

indicators.note: busy suggests frantic activity, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is working this evening as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler' suggests the setter of the crossword, but here it is someone who gathers writings.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthologist assembles an anthology, gathering selected poems or stories into one book.

clue.text: Nobel prize winner — second person in France to feature twice

parts.note: tu is the French familiar word for you

explanation.surface: A Nobel laureate appears twice in French grammar lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Desmond Tutu, the South African archbishop, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984. 'Second person' is the grammatical you.
explanation.definitionFit: Desmond Tutu received the Nobel Peace Prize for opposing apartheid, so he is an example of a laureate.

clue.text: Eastern India restricted by old regular payment

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something restricted by another is hemmed in by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: a rental is a periodic payment for use of property
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: India is held back by an old system of regular payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is a dated word for something from Asia, the East.

clue.text: Hurries holidaymaker aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on board, inside the vessel

explanation.surface: A tourist rushes to get on board a ship before it sails.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly with short steps, so scampers is a synonym for dashes.

clue.text: Musical performance from area in close to eastern direction?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the piece that follows

parts.note: east-north-east is a compass direction next to east

explanation.surface: A musical piece drifts in from somewhere off to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' seems to ask for a last letter, but it means a direction nearly east.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is a piece of music played between the acts of a stage production.

clue.text: Carbon, oxygen and phosphorus in heap forming ester?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Chemical elements piled together make an ester.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that an ester is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is a chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: What's earlier than foxtrot in dance choice?

indicators.note: in means found within the run of letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Which dance comes before the foxtrot on the programme?
explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot sounds like a dance, but it is the code word for F in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, E's code word comes just before F, which is foxtrot.

clue.text: Easy thing or easterly thing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a task done without effort
second meaning: a light wind, of which an easterly is one kind

explanation.walkthrough: An easterly is a wind from the east; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is a cinch is called this, and the word also names a gentle wind.

clue.text: Contemporary of Gates, B, to attempt firearms practice

parts.note: Bill Gates written index-style as Gates, B; his tech contemporary Elon Musk becomes Musk, E

explanation.surface: A tech tycoon tries out shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma style, surname then initial, is how names appear in an index; follow it through for the rival billionaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Musketry is the art or practice of firing muskets and other small arms.

clue.text: Poet overlooking British and our enthusiasm

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A poet who ignores Britain dampens our passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate eagerness, a synonym for enthusiasm.

clue.text: Surrounded by support, receiving millions

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it inside

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Someone amid backers gets millions in funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, so it means encircled by.

clue.text: Festival putting out special meal for me?

indicators.note: putting something out removes it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A festival lays on a special meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: if a meal is for me, I am the one consuming it.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a meal is meant for is the diner, the one who consumes the food.

clue.text: How far will five letters get you in extremity?

wordplay.words: How far will five letters get you
wordplay.note: counting five letters from A of the alphabet takes you as far as E

explanation.surface: A riddle about how far a few letters will carry you.
explanation.walkthrough: Starting from A, five letters run A, B, C, D, E: that gets you to E, written as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe is a digit at the end of the foot, one of the body's extremities.

clue.text: Aster? Write music about it

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

explanation.surface: A songwriter is asked to compose a piece about the aster flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The aster belongs to the daisy family, once called the composites because each flower head is made of many tiny florets.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists class the aster as a composite plant, its head a cluster of small florets, so it is an example.

clue.text: Metal tip — lead?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pointed head of a spear
second meaning: to head an attack or campaign

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' could be the metal itself, tempting a reading about a pencil, but here it is the verb to be in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the iron point of a spear, and as a verb it means to head a movement.

clue.text: Money returned regarding fertiliser ingredient

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: Money comes back over a matter of fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, a salt used to make fertilisers as well as gunpowder.
